title.zh: 卷九十八 列傳第二十八: 蕭兀納 耶律儼 劉伸 耶律胡呂
title.en: Volume 98 Biographies 28: Xiao Wuna, Yelu Yan, Liu Shen, Yelu Hulu
title.raw: 卷九十八 列傳第二十八: 蕭兀納 耶律儼 劉伸 耶律胡呂 Volume 98 Biographies 28: Xiao Wuna, Yelu Yan, Liu Shen, Yelu Hulu

sentences.zh: 蕭兀納耶律儼劉伸耶律胡呂

translations.literal: Xiao Wuna, Yelu Yan, Liu Shen, Yelu Hulu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Wuna, Yelu Yan, Liu Shen, and Yelu Hulu

sentences.zh: 蕭兀納，一名撻不也，字特免，六院部人。

translations.literal: Xiao Wuna, also named Tabuye, style Te Mian, a man of the Six Yuan Division.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Wuna, also known as Tabuye, courtesy name Te Mian, was from the Six Yuan Division.

sentences.zh: 其先嘗為西南面拽剌。

translations.literal: His forebear had once served as zhuala of the Southwestern Route.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor of his had once held the post of zhuala on the Southwestern Route.

sentences.zh: 兀納魁偉簡重，善騎射。

translations.literal: Wuna was tall and imposing, plain and grave, skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Wuna was tall and imposing, plainspoken and dignified, and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 清寧初，兄圖獨以事入見，帝問族人可用者，圖獨以兀納對，補祗候郎君。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, his elder brother Tuduo entered audience on business; the emperor asked which clansmen were usable, Tuduo answered with Wuna, and he was appointed attendant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingning, his elder brother Tuduo came to court on business; when the emperor asked which relatives might serve, Tuduo named Wuna, and Wuna was appointed an attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 遷近侍敞史，護衛太保。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be inner attendant recorder, then Guardian Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to inner attendant recorder and then Guardian Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 大康初，為北院宣徽使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang, he became Northern Court Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dakang he was made Northern Court Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 時乙辛巳害太子，因言宋魏國王和魯斡之子淳可為儲嗣。

translations.literal: At that time Yixin had already harmed the crown prince, and therefore proposed that Chun, son of Song Prince of Wei Heluwo, could serve as heir designate.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin had already destroyed the crown prince and now argued that Chun, son of Heluwo, Prince of Wei of Song, ought to be named heir.

sentences.zh: 群臣莫敢言，唯兀納及夷離畢蕭陶隗諫曰：「舍嫡不立，是以國與人也。」

translations.literal: None of the officials dared speak; only Wuna and Yilibi Xiao Taowei remonstrated, saying, "To set aside the legitimate heir and not establish him is to give the state to others."
translations.idiomatic: No one else among the ministers dared object; only Wuna and Yilibi Xiao Taowei spoke up: "To pass over the legitimate heir is to hand the realm to outsiders."

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫不決。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wavered, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝出獵，乙辛請留皇孫，帝欲從之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the emperor went out hunting; Yixin asked that the imperial grandson be left behind, and the emperor wished to agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor went hunting; Yixin asked to keep the imperial grandson at court, and the emperor was inclined to consent.

sentences.zh: 兀納奏曰：「竊聞車駕出遊，將留皇孫，茍保護非人，恐有他變。

translations.literal: Wuna memorialized, saying, "I have heard privately that as the imperial carriage goes out on tour, the imperial grandson is to be left behind; if protection should fall to the wrong men, I fear there may be some other turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: Wuna memorialized: "I understand Your Majesty is about to leave on tour while keeping the imperial grandson behind; if unsuitable men are charged with his protection, I fear disaster.

sentences.zh: 果留，臣請侍左右。」

translations.literal: If he is indeed left behind, your subject requests to wait at his side."
translations.idiomatic: If he stays behind, I beg leave to attend him in person."

sentences.zh: 帝乃悟，命皇孫從行。

translations.literal: The emperor then understood and ordered the imperial grandson to accompany the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his meaning and ordered the grandson to come along.

sentences.zh: 由此始疑乙辛。

translations.literal: From this he first grew suspicious of Yixin.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the emperor began to doubt Yixin.

sentences.zh: 頃之，同知南院樞密使事，出乙辛、淳等。

translations.literal: Before long, as vice administrator of the Southern Chancellery Privy Council, he banished Yixin, Chun, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, serving as vice administrator of the Southern Chancellery Privy Council, he drove Yixin, Chun, and their faction from court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其忠，封蘭陵郡王，人謂近於古社稷臣。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty, enfeoffed him Prince of Lanling Commandery, and people said he approached the ancient type of minister of state and altars.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty and enfeoffed him as Prince of Lanling; contemporaries said he resembled the loyal ministers of old who saved dynasties.

sentences.zh: 授殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Inspector of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Inspector of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 上謂王師儒、耶律固等曰：「兀納忠純，雖狄仁傑輔唐，屋質立穆宗，無以過也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wang Shiru, Yelu Gu, and the others, "Wuna is loyal and pure; even Di Renjie assisting Tang, or Wuzhi establishing Muzong—none surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wang Shiru, Yelu Gu, and others: "Wuna's loyalty is unstained. Not even Di Renjie's service to Tang, or Yelu Wuzhi's elevation of Muzong, exceeds what he has done.

sentences.zh: 卿等宜達燕王知之。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen should convey this to the Prince of Yan so that he knows."
translations.idiomatic: Tell the Prince of Yan, so that he knows how highly I esteem this."

sentences.zh: 自是令兀納輔導燕王，益見優寵。

translations.literal: From then on Wuna was ordered to guide and instruct the Prince of Yan, and he received still greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wuna was assigned to guide the Prince of Yan and received even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 大安初，詔尚越國公主，兀納固辭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an, an edict ordered him to marry the Princess of Yue, and Wuna firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Da'an he was commanded to marry the Princess of Yue, but Wuna steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 改南院樞密使，奏請掾史宜以歲月行敘，從之。

translations.literal: He was changed to Southern Chancellery Privy Commissioner; he memorialized that clerks should advance by length of service, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Southern Chancellery Privy Commissioner and proposed that staff clerks be promoted according to seniority; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 壽隆元年，拜北府宰相。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shoulong, he was appointed chancellor of the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Shoulong 1 he was appointed chancellor of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 初，天祚在潛邸，兀納數以直言忤旨。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tianzuo was still in the Hidden Residence, Wuna several times spoke bluntly and offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: While Tianzuo was still heir apparent, Wuna often spoke bluntly and offended him.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，出為遼興軍節度使，守太傅。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Wuna was sent out as military commissioner of Liaoxing Army, with the added title Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tianzuo took the throne, Wuna was sent out as military commissioner of Liaoxing Army with the honorary title Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 以佛殿小底王華誣兀納借內府犀角，詔鞫之。

translations.literal: Because Buddhist Hall attendant Wang Hua falsely accused Wuna of borrowing rhinoceros horn from the inner treasury, an edict ordered investigation.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant named Wang Hua falsely accused Wuna of having borrowed rhinoceros horn from the imperial stores, and an edict ordered an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 兀納奏曰：「臣在先朝，詔許日取帑錢十萬為私費，臣未嘗妄取一錢，肯借犀角乎！」

translations.literal: Wuna memorialized, saying, "Your subject, under the former reign, was permitted by edict to take one hundred thousand from the treasury daily for private expenses, yet never took a single coin inappropriately—would I borrow rhinoceros horn!"
translations.idiomatic: Wuna replied: "Under the previous reign I was allowed one hundred thousand strings a day from the treasury for personal expenses, yet I never took a coin I was not owed—why would I borrow rhinoceros horn?"

sentences.zh: 天祚愈怒，奪太傅官，降寧邊州刺史，尋改臨海軍節度使。

translations.literal: Tianzuo grew still angrier, stripped him of the Grand Mentor title, demoted him to prefect of Ningbian, and soon changed him to military commissioner of Linhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo was only enraged the more: he stripped Wuna of Grand Mentor, demoted him to prefect of Ningbian, and soon afterward transferred him to military commissioner of Linhai Army.

sentences.zh: 兀納上書曰：「自蕭海裏亡入女直，彼有輕朝廷心，宜益兵以備不虞。」

translations.literal: Wuna submitted a memorial, saying, "Since Xiao Haili fled into the Jurchen, they hold the court in contempt; troops should be increased to guard against the unexpected."
translations.idiomatic: Wuna wrote: "Since Xiao Haili defected to the Jurchen, they have begun to hold the court in contempt. We should reinforce the frontier before trouble arrives."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 天慶元年，知黃龍府事，改東北路統軍使，復上書曰：「臣治與女直接境，觀其所為，其志非小。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqing, he governed affairs at Huanglong Prefecture; he was changed to commander-in-chief of the Northeast Route and again submitted a memorial, saying, "The territory I administer borders the Jurchen directly; judging by their conduct, their ambition is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqing 1 he was assigned to Huanglong Prefecture, then made commander-in-chief of the Northeast Route. He wrote again: "My jurisdiction borders the Jurchen directly, and from what I observe their ambitions are far from modest.

sentences.zh: 宜先其未發，舉兵圖之。」

translations.literal: We ought, before they act, to raise troops and plan against them."
translations.idiomatic: We should strike before they rise."

sentences.zh: 章數上，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Memorial after memorial went up; none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He sent memorial after memorial; none were heeded.

sentences.zh: 及金兵來侵，戰於寧江州，其孫移敵蹇死之，兀納退走入城。

translations.literal: When Jin forces came to invade, fighting at Ningjiang Prefecture, his grandson Yidiqian died in battle, and Wuna retreated and fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked and battle was joined at Ningjiang, his grandson Yidiqian was killed; Wuna fell back into the city.

sentences.zh: 留官屬守禦，自以三百騎渡混同江而西，城遂陷。

translations.literal: He left subordinates to defend, himself crossed the Huntong River westward with three hundred horsemen, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving his staff to hold the walls, he himself crossed the Huntong River westward with three hundred horsemen—and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 後與蕭敵裏拒金兵於長濼，以軍敗免官。

translations.literal: Later, together with Xiao Dili he resisted Jin forces at Changli Marsh and was dismissed from office when the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Xiao Dili, he tried to hold the Jin at Changli Marsh; when the army was routed he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 五年，天祚親征，兀納殿，復敗績。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Tianzuo personally campaigned; Wuna served in the rear guard and again suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Tianzuo took the field in person; Wuna commanded the rear guard and was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 後數日乃與百官入見，授上京留守。

translations.literal: Several days later he entered audience with the hundred officials and was appointed regent of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Some days later he appeared at court with the other officials and was appointed regent of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 六年，耶律章奴叛，來攻京城，兀納發府庫以賚士卒，諭以逆順，完城池，以死拒戰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yelu Zhangnu rebelled and came to attack the capital city; Wuna opened the treasury to reward the soldiers, explained right and rebellion, repaired the walls, and resisted with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Yelu Zhangnu rebelled and marched on the capital; Wuna opened the treasury to pay the troops, appealed to them on loyalty and treason, strengthened the walls, and fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 章奴無所得而去。

translations.literal: Zhangnu gained nothing and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangnu withdrew without gain.

sentences.zh: 以功授副元帥，尋為契丹都宮使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed vice commander-in-chief, and soon became Khitan Director of the Palace Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made vice commander-in-chief, and soon afterward Director of the Khitan Palace Establishment.

sentences.zh: 天祚以兀納先朝重臣，有定策勛，每延問以政，兀納對甚切。

translations.literal: Tianzuo, because Wuna was a great minister of the former reign with merit in settling the succession, repeatedly summoned him to discuss government, and Wuna answered very forthrightly.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo, mindful that Wuna was a senior minister of Daozong's reign who had helped settle the succession, often consulted him on policy; Wuna answered without reserve.

sentences.zh: 上雖優容，終不能用。

translations.literal: Although the emperor treated him indulgently, in the end his counsel was never adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened politely but never acted on what he said.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died of illness at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at seventy.

sentences.zh: 耶律儼，字若思，析津人。

translations.literal: Yelu Yan, style Ruosi, a man of Xijin.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Yan, courtesy name Ruosi, was a native of Xijin.

sentences.zh: 本姓李氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Li.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from the Li clan.

sentences.zh: 父仲禧，重熙中始仕。

translations.literal: His father Zhongxi first entered office in Chongxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongxi entered government service during Chongxi.

sentences.zh: 清寧初，同知南院宣徽使事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingning, he served as vice commissioner of Southern Court Imperial Household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingning he became vice commissioner of the Southern Court Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 四年，城鴨子、混同二水間，拜北院宣徽使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he walled the area between the Yazi and Huntong rivers and was appointed Northern Court Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he fortified the junction of the Yazi and Huntong Rivers and was promoted to Northern Court Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 咸雍初，坐誤奏事，出為榆州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianyong, for mistakenly memorializing a matter he was sent out as prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianyong he was demoted to prefect of Yuzhou for a faulty memorial.

sentences.zh: 俄詔復舊職，遷漢人行宮都部署。

translations.literal: Before long an edict restored his former post, and he was transferred to be Overall Deployment commissioner of the Han Mobile Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to his former post and made Overall Deployment commissioner of the Han mobile palace.

sentences.zh: 六年，賜國姓，封韓國公，改南院樞密使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was granted the imperial surname, enfeoffed Duke of Han, and changed to Southern Chancellery Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he received the imperial surname Yelu, was enfeoffed Duke of Han, and made Southern Chancellery Privy Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時樞臣乙辛等誣陷皇太子，詔仲禧偕乙辛鞫之，蔓引無辜，未嘗雪正。

translations.literal: At that time Privy Councilor Yixin and others falsely implicated the crown prince; an edict ordered Zhongxi together with Yixin to investigate, implicating the innocent in widening chains, and never clearing what was right.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixin and his faction framed the crown prince, Zhongxi was ordered to investigate alongside Yixin; the inquiry spread falsely to the innocent and never cleared the prince's name.

sentences.zh: 乙辛薦仲禧可任，拜廣德軍節度使，復為南院樞密使，卒，謚欽惠。

translations.literal: Yixin recommended Zhongxi as capable; he was appointed military commissioner of Guangde Army, again Southern Chancellery Privy Commissioner, died, and was posthumously titled Qinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin praised Zhongxi's reliability; he was made military commissioner of Guangde Army and again Southern Privy Commissioner, and died with the posthumous title Qinhui.

sentences.zh: 儼儀觀秀整，好學，有詩名，登咸雍進士第。

translations.literal: Yan's bearing and appearance were elegant and fine; he loved learning, had a reputation in poetry, and passed the Xianyong jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was handsome and well composed, devoted to learning, and celebrated as a poet; he passed the jinshi examination in Xianyong.

sentences.zh: 守著作佐郎，補中書省令史，以勤敏稱。

translations.literal: He served as Assistant Director of the Bureau of Attendants, was appointed secretariat clerk of the Central Secretariat, and was known for diligence and alertness.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an assistant in the Bureau of Attendants and then as a secretariat clerk, praised for diligence and quickness.

sentences.zh: 大康初，歷都部署判官、將作少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang he successively held posts as Overall Deployment judge and Vice Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dakang he served as Overall Deployment judge and then as Vice Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 後兩府奏事，論群臣優劣，唯稱儼才俊。

translations.literal: Later, when the two chancelleries reported on affairs, discussing the merits and flaws of the hundred officials, only Yan was called talented and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the two chancelleries reviewed the ministers, only Yan was singled out as exceptionally able.

sentences.zh: 改少府少監，知大理正，賜紫。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Palace Workshop, made Director of the Court of Justice, and granted purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Palace Workshop and acting director of the Court of Justice, and awarded the purple official robe.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷大理少卿，奏讞詳平。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Justice; his memorials on cases were detailed and even.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Justice; his judgments were thorough and fair.

sentences.zh: 明年，升大理卿。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，奪服，同簽部署司事。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his father, mourning garments were stripped from him, and he served jointly signing Deployment Office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was recalled from mourning to serve jointly in the Deployment Office.

sentences.zh: 大安初，為景州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he became prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Da'an he was appointed prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 繩胥徒，禁豪猾，撫老恤貧，未數月，善政流播，郡人刻石頌德。

translations.literal: He restrained clerks and runners, forbade powerful bullies, comforted the aged and pitied the poor; within a few months good government spread abroad, and the commandery people carved stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined petty officials, checked the powerful, and cared for the old and poor; within months his good rule was famed throughout the prefecture, and the people carved a stone in his honor.

sentences.zh: 二年，改御史中丞，詔按上京滯獄，多所平反。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to Censor-in-Chief; by edict he reviewed stagnant cases at the Upper Capital, and many wrongful verdicts were overturned.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he became Censor-in-Chief and was ordered to review backlogged cases at the Upper Capital, reversing many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 同知宣徽院事，提點大理寺。

translations.literal: He was vice administrator of the Imperial Household Office and supervising director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice administrator of the Imperial Household Office and supervising director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，改山西路都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, winter, he was changed to Overall Transport Commissioner of the Western Shanxi Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year six he became Overall Transport Commissioner of the Western Shanxi Route.

sentences.zh: 刮剔垢弊，奏定課額，益州縣俸給，事皆施行。

translations.literal: He scraped away grime and abuses, memorialized to fix tax quotas, increased prefecture and county salaries, and all matters were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He cleaned out abuses, fixed tax quotas, and raised county and prefecture salaries; his reforms were all enacted.

sentences.zh: 壽隆初，授樞密直學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shoulong he was granted Privy Council Academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shoulong he was made Privy Council Academician.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官，尋召復舊職。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he left office; before long he was summoned and restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother but was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 宋攻夏，李乾順遣使求和解，帝命儼如宋平之，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Song attacked Xia; Li Qianshun sent envoys seeking reconciliation; the emperor ordered Yan to go to Song to settle it, and he was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Song attacked Western Xia, Li Qianshun of Xia sent envoys seeking peace; the emperor dispatched Yan to mediate with Song, and on his return Yan was made Associate Administrator of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，駕幸鴛鴦濼，召至內殿，訪以政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, as the carriage visited Yuanyang Marsh, he was summoned to the inner hall and consulted on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the emperor visited Yuanyang Marsh, summoned Yan to the inner hall, and questioned him on policy.

sentences.zh: 儼素廉潔，一芥不取於人。

translations.literal: Yan by nature was incorrupt and pure; he would not take even a mustard seed from others.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was incorruptible by nature and would accept nothing, not even the smallest gift, from anyone.

sentences.zh: 經籍一覽成誦。

translations.literal: Classical texts, one glance and he could recite them.
translations.idiomatic: He could read a classical text once and recite it from memory.

sentences.zh: 又善伺人主意。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at reading others' intentions.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at reading the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 妻邢氏有美色，常出入禁中，儼教之曰：「慎勿失上意。」

translations.literal: His wife Lady Xing had beautiful looks and often entered and left the forbidden precincts; Yan instructed her, saying, "Be careful never to lose the emperor's favor."
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Xing, was beautiful and frequently entered the inner palace; Yan told her: "Take care never to displease the emperor."

sentences.zh: 由是權寵益固。

translations.literal: By this his power and favor grew firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: By this means their influence at court grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 三子：處貞，太常少卿；

translations.literal: Three sons: Chuzhen, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Chuzhen, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 處廉，同知中京留守事；

translations.literal: Chulian, vice regent of the Central Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Chulian, vice regent of the Central Capital;

sentences.zh: 處能，少府少監。

translations.literal: Chuneng, Vice Director of the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: and Chuneng, Vice Director of the Palace Workshop.

sentences.zh: 劉伸，字濟時，宛平人。

translations.literal: Liu Shen, style Jishi, a man of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen, courtesy name Jishi, was from Wanping.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟，長以辭翰聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and perceptive; grown, he was known for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted as a youth, he later won renown for his writing.

sentences.zh: 重熙五年，登進士第，歷彰武軍節度使掌書記、大理正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongxi he passed the jinshi examination, and successively served as recorder to the military commissioner of Zhangwu Army and Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongxi 5 he passed the jinshi examination and served as recorder to the Zhangwu Army military commissioner and then as director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 因奏獄，上適與近臣語，不顧，伸進曰：「臣聞自古帝王必重民命，願陛下省臣之奏。

translations.literal: While reporting on cases, the emperor happened to be speaking with close ministers and paid no attention; Shen stepped forward and said, "Your subject has heard that from antiquity emperors and kings must heavily regard the people's lives; I pray Your Majesty will attend to your subject's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Once while presenting a case report the emperor was chatting with courtiers and ignored him; Shen stepped forward: "Since antiquity wise rulers have held the people's lives sacred; I beg Your Majesty to hear my report.

sentences.zh: 「上大驚異，擢樞密都承旨，權中京副留守。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly startled and impressed, promoted him to chief usher of the Privy Council, and acting vice regent of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished, promoted him to chief usher of the Privy Council, and acting vice regent of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 詔徙富民以實春、泰二州，伸以為不可，奏罷之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered wealthy households moved to populate Chun and Tai Prefectures; Shen held this wrong and memorialized to cancel it.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered wealthy households relocated to populate Chun and Tai Prefectures, Shen objected and had the order revoked.

sentences.zh: 遷大理少卿，人以不冤。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Justice; people said no one suffered wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Justice, he was known for leaving no one wrongfully condemned.

sentences.zh: 升大理卿，改西京副留守。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Director of the Court of Justice and changed to vice regent of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Court of Justice and then became vice regent of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 以父憂，終制，為三司副使，加諫議大夫，提點大理寺。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his father, after completing the mourning period he became Vice Commissioner of the Three Bureaus, with the added title Remonstrance Grandee, and supervising director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his father, he served as Vice Commissioner of the Three Bureaus with the added title Remonstrance Grandee and as supervising director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以伸明法而恕，案冤獄全活者眾，徙南京副留守。

translations.literal: Because Shen understood law yet was forgiving, in cases of wrongful imprisonment many lives were wholly spared; he was transferred to vice regent of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Known for mastery of the law and merciful judgment, he saved many from false imprisonment, and was transferred to vice regent of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 俄改崇義軍節度使，政務簡靜，民用不擾，致烏鵲同巢之異，優詔褒之。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to military commissioner of Chongyi Army; government affairs were simple and quiet, the people's livelihood undisturbed, producing the prodigy of crows and magpies nesting together, and an excellent edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became military commissioner of Chongyi Army; his rule was calm and unobtrusive, the people untroubled, and crows and magpies were seen nesting together—a portent of peace for which he received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 改戶部使，歲入羨余錢三十萬緡，拜南院樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Households Commissioner; annual surplus money of three hundred thousand strings was submitted, and he was appointed Southern Chancellery Vice Privy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Households Commissioner he delivered three hundred thousand strings in annual surplus and was promoted to vice privy commissioner of the Southern Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 道宗嘗謂大臣曰：「今之忠直，耶律玦、劉伸而已！」

translations.literal: Daozong once told his great ministers, "Among those loyal and upright today, only Yelu Jue and Liu Shen!"
translations.idiomatic: Daozong once told his ministers: "Today only Yelu Jue and Liu Shen are truly loyal and upright!"

sentences.zh: 宰相楊績賀其得人。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yang Ji congratulated him on getting the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yang Ji praised him for recognizing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「卿勿憚宰相。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him, saying, "You, sir, need not fear the chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "Do not hold back for fear of the chancellor."

sentences.zh: 時北院樞密使乙辛勢焰方熾，伸奏曰：「臣於乙辛尚不畏，何宰相之畏！」

translations.literal: At that time Northern Chancellery Privy Commissioner Yixin's power and flame were just blazing; Shen memorialized, saying, "Your subject does not even fear Yixin—why fear the chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: Yixin, Northern Privy Commissioner, was at the height of his power; Shen replied: "If I do not fear Yixin, why should I fear the chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 乙辛銜之，相與排詆，出為保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: Yixin harbored resentment; together they slandered and drove him out as military commissioner of Baojing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin took offense; he and his allies smeared Shen and had him sent out as military commissioner of Baojing Army.

sentences.zh: 上終欲大用，加守太子太保，遷上京留守。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end wished to employ him greatly; he was given the added title Guardian Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to regent of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still meant to use him at the highest level: Shen was given the honorary title Guardian Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and made regent of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙辛以事徙鎮雄武，復以崇義軍節度使致仕。

translations.literal: Yixin, because of a matter, was transferred to command Xiongwu; Shen again retired with the rank of military commissioner of Chongyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin was transferred to Xiongwu on account of his offenses; Liu Shen retired once more, retaining the honorary rank of military commissioner of Chongyi Army.

sentences.zh: 適燕、薊民饑，伸與致政趙徽、韓造日濟以糜粥，所活不勝算。

translations.literal: When Yan and Ji peoples suffered famine, Shen together with retired Zhao Hui and Han Zao daily supplied porridge; those saved cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Just then famine struck Yan and Ji; Shen, together with the retired officials Zhao Hui and Han Zao, distributed porridge daily and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 大安二年卒，上震悼，賻贈加等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Da'an he died; the emperor was shaken and grieved, and funeral gifts and posthumous rewards were increased by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an 2 he died; the emperor was deeply grieved and granted enhanced funeral gifts and posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 耶律胡呂，字蘇撒，弘義宮分人。

translations.literal: Yelu Hulu, style Susa, a man of the Hongyi Palace Division.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Hulu, courtesy name Susa, was from the Hongyi Palace Division.

sentences.zh: 其先欲穩，佐太祖有功，為叠烈部夷離堇。

translations.literal: His forebear Yiwen assisted Taizu with merit and was yilijin of the Dielie Division.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Yiwen had aided Taizu with distinction and served as yilijin of the Dielie Division.

sentences.zh: 父楊五，左監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Yang Wu, General of the Left Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang Wu was a general of the Left Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 胡呂性謙謹，於人無適莫。

translations.literal: Hulu by nature was modest and careful; toward people he had no favoring or shunning.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu was modest and careful by nature and showed no partiality toward anyone.

sentences.zh: 重熙末，補寢殿小底。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongxi he was appointed sleeping-hall attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Chongxi he was appointed a sleeping-hall attendant.

sentences.zh: 以善職，屢更華要，遷千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: For excellence in office he repeatedly changed to splendid and important posts, and was promoted to General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For distinguished service he rose through one prestigious post after another and was promoted to general of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 大安中，北阻卜酋磨魯斯叛，為招討都監，與耶律那也率精騎二千討平之，以功為漢人行宮副部署，兼知太和宮事。

translations.literal: In Da'an, the Northern Zhubu chieftain Molusi rebelled; he served as overall pacification supervising commissioner, together with Yelu Naye led two thousand picked horsemen to suppress and pacify them, and for merit became vice deployment commissioner of the Han Mobile Court, concurrently administering Taihe Palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Da'an the Northern Zhubu chieftain Molusi rebelled; Hulu served as supervising commissioner of the pacification campaign and, with Yelu Naye, led two thousand picked horsemen to crush the revolt; for this he was made vice deployment commissioner of the Han mobile palace and concurrently administrator of Taihe Palace.

sentences.zh: 致仕，加同中書門下平章事，卒。

translations.literal: He retired, was given the added title Co-Seal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the added title of Co-Seal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and later died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：兀納當道宗昏惑之會，擁佑皇孫，使乙辛奸計不獲復逞，而遼祚以續，比之屋質立穆宗，非溢美也。

translations.literal: Comment: Wuna, at the time when Daozong was confused and deluded, supported and protected the imperial grandson, causing Yixin's treacherous scheme not to obtain display again, and the Liao line thereby continued—compared to Wuzhi establishing Muzong, this is no excess of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: At a moment when Daozong had lost his judgment, Wuna protected the imperial grandson and blocked Yixin's treachery from running its course, thereby preserving the Liao succession. To compare him with Yelu Wuzhi's elevation of Muzong is no flattery.

sentences.zh: 儼以俊才蒞政，所至有能譽，纂述遼史，具一代治亂，亦云勤矣，但其固寵，不能以禮正家，惜哉。

translations.literal: Yan, with outstanding talent administering government, wherever he arrived had reputation for ability; compiling and describing the History of Liao, fully treating one generation's order and chaos, may also be called diligent—but his securing favor, unable to correct the household by ritual, alas.
translations.idiomatic: Yan governed with outstanding talent and won a reputation for competence wherever he served; his compilation of the History of Liao, recording an entire age of order and disorder, shows real diligence as well—yet he secured imperial favor by means his wife's conduct in the inner palace rather than by keeping his household in ritual order. A pity.

sentences.zh: 劉伸三為大理，民無冤抑，一登戶部，上下兼裕，至與耶律玦並稱忠直，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: Liu Shen thrice served at the Court of Justice, the people without wronged oppression; one ascent to the Households Bureau, upper and lower both ample; reaching being named together with Yelu Jue as loyal and upright—is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen thrice held the Court of Justice and left the people free of wrongful oppression; once at the head of the Households Bureau he filled both imperial and local coffers; that he should stand with Yelu Jue among the loyal and upright—is that not exactly as it should be?
